note: The buying committee. Sourced from Forrester's Buying Networks vision report (April 2025) and Buyers' Journey Survey 2024, presented at B2B Summit. Kept deliberately short — this is orientation, not a course.
headline: You are not selling to a person. You are selling to about 22 of them, and nine are outside the building.

shape.label: people inside the organization
shape.detail: The buying group. These are the ones your champion has to carry.

shape.label: people outside it
shape.detail: Peers, consultants, analysts, communities, partners. You will never meet most of them.

shape.label: of purchases stall
shape.detail: The most common competitor is not another vendor. It is the deal stopping.

shape.label: end up dissatisfied
shape.detail: Even with the provider they chose. Buyers know this, which is why they hesitate.

trust.headline: Who they believe, in order

spheres.name: Core insiders
spheres.what: Firsthand and directly connected. Coworkers, management, and the vendors they already run.

spheres.name: Independent experts
spheres.what: Authoritative voices with privileged insight. Peers, analysts, consultants, other customers.

spheres.name: Outsiders
spheres.what: Tertiary sources with a visible self-interest. This is where a salesperson sits.

trust.soWhat: A rep is the least-trusted voice a buyer has, at 58%. Forrester files salespeople under outsiders — alongside news media and influencers. Arguing a point harder does not move it. A peer, a customer reference, or a benchmark does.
trust.theIncumbentProblem: The one that should change how you sell: **the vendor they already run is trusted at 79%** — above industry peers, above analysts, and 21 points above you. So when Yardi or RealPage says "we do training too," that lands as a trusted insider. Your rebuttal lands as an outsider. That is not a messaging problem, it is a structural one, and it is exactly why consolidation is our single biggest loss reason. Do not out-argue the incumbent. Ask the buyer to check one specific, verifiable thing — the state approval list, the CE credit, who updates the content when the law changes.

ai.headline: AI is now in the buying committee
points: 87% of buyers used genAI in a purchase in the last year. 95% expect to next year.
GenAI is the second most impactful interaction they have — ahead of talking to a salesperson.
38% use it to research specific vendors. 32% use it to compare vendor strengths and weaknesses. 23% use it to build the shortlist.
ai.soWhat: A model is comparing us to Yardi before a rep gets a meeting, using whatever is publicly findable. What our website and third-party sources say is now a competitive surface, not a marketing one.

committee.wants: To look right for backing this
committee.give: The internal case, in their language, that they can forward without editing
A number and a timeframe. Not a feature list

committee.who: IT or whoever owns the PMS relationship
committee.give: Where we sit relative to the PMS, and what we do not try to replace

committee.wants: No more work landing on site teams
committee.give: What changes for the person on site, honestly
Clear packaging, so they are not forced to compare on price alone

plays: Ask who else has to say yes, and what each of them would need to see. Most reps ask who the decision maker is and stop there.
Assume nine people you will never meet are being consulted. Give the champion something forwardable — a benchmark, a peer example, a one-pager — rather than a conversation only they heard.
When a deal goes quiet, treat the stall as the competitor. 86% of purchases stall; the question is which of the 22 has an unanswered objection, not whether a rival is winning.
Never fight the trust ranking. If they doubt a claim, reach for a customer, a benchmark or a third party. A rep repeating it louder is the least persuasive option available.
source: Forrester, Buying Networks: Your Buyers' New Reality, April 2025 · Who Do B2B Buyers Trust?, B2B Summit 2025 · Business Trust Survey 2023 (1,420 global business buyers) · Buyers' Journey Survey 2024

generations.headline: Who is in the room has changed
generations.mixNote: 59% of buying-group members are now digital natives. Two-thirds of buyers on $1M+ purchases are Millennial or Gen Z.
generations.soWhat: For the majority of the room, generative AI is the single most preferred way to learn about a vendor — ahead of talking to a person. For the older third, a product expert still wins and a rep comes second. Same deal, two different front doors.

generations.lateSoWhat: By the time a rep is in the conversation, the shortlist is usually set. The competitive work that matters most happens before anyone picks up the phone — in what is publicly findable about us.
